reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and date adjustment helpers, but implements daily occurrence eligibility separately in getNextDate and getDatesInRange.

duplication.why: Daily skipping policy and the weekend-or-holiday predicate are repeated across occurrence selection, range enumeration, and date adjustment.

placement.why: Handler registration and model changes fit their layers, but the range handler owns scheduling policy that belongs alongside the shared scheduling helpers.

scope.why: All edits concern the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration field, or their tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate multiple eligibility implementations and range-padding assumptions, while existing adjustment consumers remain outside the shared daily-skipping policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts:getDatesInRange independently implements daily eligibility instead of sharing the policy introduced in shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: Daily weekend/holiday exclusion is expressed as an occurrence-advancing loop in getNextDate and an array filter in getDatesInRange; both repeat the eligibility decision.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithWeekendRule gains holidays; getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch; getDatesInRange reimplements daily eligibility, while getUpcomingDates and both schedule-template adjustment calls bypass that daily policy.
